grounded_against: phase3/evaluation/metrics/{retrieval,evidence,provenance,equivalence,selection}.py and phase3/evaluation/agent/outcomes.py, read directly in this stage

metrics.recall_at_k: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, upgraded classification confidence after J.2 -- now 97.0% of individual evidence spans / 94.8% of items fully resolved (up from 72.5%/63.4% in J.1); NOT_ATTEMPTABLE only for the residual 2.3% zero-resolved items, which must be excluded up front (never silently scored as recall=0 against a fabricated empty gold set -- an empty gold set is a different failure mode than 'no evidence exists', per Strict-TSR's own semantics). Still classified PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, not FULLY_SUPPORTED, because a genuine (if now small) unresolvable population remains and Strict TSR's own canonical definition treats an incomplete-gold-set dataset as not fully supportable dataset-wide (Part 12, phase document).
metrics.reciprocal_rank / mean_reciprocal_rank: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, same basis as recall_at_k, same J.2 coverage upgrade.
metrics.evidence_precision / evidence_recall / e: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, same basis. Ambiguity is now explicitly quantified (not merely flagged as an open question): 88/144,598 spans (0.06%) are TRUNCATED_AMBIGUOUS/MULTIMESSAGE_AMBIGUOUS and are excluded from gold sets rather than guessed -- see reports/evidence_audit_j2.md.
metrics.redundancy / selection_count / selection: SUPPORTED -- generic over any ID sequence, no dataset-specific precondition.
metrics.strict_tsr: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, same basis as recall_at_k (now on a much larger resolvable population); genuinely NOT_ATTEMPTABLE (not merely unavailable) for the residual 2.3% zero-resolved items -- there is no gold evidence at all to check selection against for those. Strict TSR's own canonical definition (`set(selected) & set(gold_evidence) != ∅`) is UNCHANGED by this stage -- see Part 12 of the phase document.
metrics.validate_parent_edges / orphan_parent_co: NOT_ATTEMPTABLE -- no parent_ids/equivalent_to edges anywhere (full scan). Shared gap with all 7 existing MAMBench datasets, not ConvoMem-specific.
metrics.evaluate_answer_correctness (agent/outco: SUPPORTED as-is -- exact-match after .strip() only, no fuzzy comparison; works for ConvoMem's plain-string answers (100% non-null, full scan) EXCEPT abstention items, where the fixed sentence answer means exact-match works cleanly there too as long as the evaluator is not additionally asked to also verify non-abstention on an abstention item (a scoring-design question for whoever activates this dataset, not a framework gap).
metrics.answer_abstention_correctness (NOT an ex: The `category` field (preserved verbatim in every normalized task record) lets a future evaluator distinguish abstention items from non-abstention items BEFORE scoring, so 'correctly abstained' vs. 'wrong answer' need not be conflated -- but no existing metric function currently reads `category` to apply this distinction automatically. This is a real, narrow, justified candidate for a small additive framework extension IF ConvoMem is activated (not built in this stage).

implicit_connections_note: Confirmed NOT a new metric requirement (see profile's implicit_connections_capability) -- existing multi-ID evidence-recall/Recall@K handle a >1-gold-ID case natively; implicit_connection_evidence's multi-hop character is a property of the QUESTION's difficulty, not of the metric's shape.
